# Requirements Quality Checklist: Safety behaviour and scope equivalence

**Purpose**: Validate that the spec's safety behaviours and its scope-equivalence claim are written well enough to implement and to review — complete, unambiguous, mutually consistent, and objectively verifiable

**Created**: 2026-09-03

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Observability of Safety Behaviour

The feature's safety guarantees are mostly statements that **nothing happened**. A requirement whose success and failure look identical from outside cannot be reviewed, cannot be tested, and cannot fail loudly — this category exists because the user named it as the first focus area.

- [ ] CHK001 Is each "left byte-identical" requirement stated as an observable property of the file, rather than as an absence of action? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK002 Do the requirements distinguish "no standard applied" from "a standard applied and changed nothing"? Both leave the file identical, but only one indicates the feature ran. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK003 Is there a requirement making the deleted-file, non-existent-file, outside-the-repository and non-regular-file outcomes distinguishable from the feature silently failing to run at all? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK004 Does §FR-008 collapse four distinct causes into one outcome, and is that deliberate? If a reviewer cannot tell which of the four occurred, is that acceptable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the no-repeat-formatting requirement expressed as something checkable, rather than as a claim about a mechanism? "MUST NOT cause formatting to be attempted again" is only verifiable if attempts are countable. [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK006 Is a bound specified on how many times a single modification may cause a standard to run — exactly once per governing standard, or merely "not unboundedly"? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the required contents of a failure report enumerated precisely enough that a report could be judged incomplete? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "in enough detail to diagnose the cause, correct it, and try again" reducible to a checkable property, or does it rest on reviewer judgement? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the audience of each output specified — which reports reach the contributor and which reach the session — given that §FR-011 and §FR-012 name different recipients? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the visible-not-silent requirement for unavailable tooling stated in a way that could be shown unmet? [Measurability, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "MUST NOT read or write anything outside this repository" scoped to say what counts as outside — resolved symlink targets, the parent of the repository root, a second worktree of the same repository? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]

## Scope Equivalence — the "nothing changed coverage" claim

The exclusion half asserts that moving where exclusions are declared changes no check's coverage. That assertion is the feature's central correctness claim, and the user named its precision as the second focus area.

- [ ] CHK012 Is the equivalence claim stated per check, rather than in aggregate? A path lost by one check and gained by another would satisfy an aggregate claim. [Clarity, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the object of comparison defined — the set of excluded paths, or the resulting file list each check receives? These differ when two exclusions overlap or when a pattern language does. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-024, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK014 Does §FR-025's "demonstrated mechanically" specify what artifact the demonstration produces, and whether it survives as a repeatable check or is a one-off? [Gap, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for the case where two declaration formats cannot express the same exclusion — one is glob-based and another pattern-based? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 Is it specified what happens if the before/after comparison finds a difference — is the difference a defect to fix, or grounds for amending the equivalence claim? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK017 Is "exactly one place" defined per check, or per repository? A shared declaration read by two checks would satisfy one reading and not the other. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK018 For the check whose tool offers no declaration mechanism, is "somewhere a reader can find from that check alone" given a testable criterion? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK019 Is §FR-026's "cannot be able to leave the repository in a state where two declarations disagree" a property of the design, or an outcome to be enforced? If the former, is it stated as such? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements specified for a path that must be excluded from several checks — is repeating it in each declaration intended, and is that repetition distinguished from the duplication this feature removes? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §FR-021, §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the requirement to correct superseding documents specific about which documents and which earlier requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029]

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a file governed by two rewriting standards, beyond fixing their order — specifically, what happens if the second undoes the first? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the set of standards that "can rewrite a file" versus "can only report" documented anywhere in the requirements, or only assumed known? [Gap, Assumption, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for what happens when a standard rewrites a file into a state another standard would reject? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 Is there a requirement covering the single-file capability's behaviour on a path that is excluded or unsupported, as distinct from the automatic path's behaviour? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for how the shared configuration reaches a contributor who has not opted into it — is the behaviour on by default for everyone working in the repository? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK027 Is there a requirement stating that this feature must not be deliverable to consumers, expressed as a checkable property of what the repository publishes? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK028 Do §FR-003 and the whole exclusion half conflict, given that the latter edits every standard's configuration? Is the distinction between changing a configuration and relocating a declaration stated? [Conflict, Spec §FR-003, §FR-021] — **Resolved 2026-09-03**: FR-003 rewritten to forbid changing what a standard requires and which paths it excludes, and to state explicitly that relocating a declaration is not such a change, deferring the equivalence to FR-024.
- [x] CHK029 Are §FR-017 and §FR-028 consistent? Removing a check changes what the aggregate does. [Conflict, Spec §FR-017, §FR-028] — **Resolved 2026-09-03**: FR-017 rewritten to scope its guarantee to the checks that survive, to restate the aggregate's stop-at-first-failure and status-passthrough behaviour, and to name the removed check as the one intended difference.
- [ ] CHK030 Is the terminology consistent across both halves — "standard", "check", and "quality check" appear to name the same thing; is one canonical? [Terminology, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK031 Do the two user stories' Independent Test statements agree with the success criteria that cover them? [Consistency, Spec §SC-002, §SC-004]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK032 Is SC-002's "byte-for-byte identical" defined over an ordered or unordered file list? Two runs of a file-listing operation need not agree on order. [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK033 Is SC-003's "exactly one edit, down from six" verifiable, or is it a description of intent? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK034 Does SC-005 enumerate seven cases while the edge-case list and §FR-008 group them differently? Is the mapping between them stated? [Consistency, Spec §SC-005, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK035 Is SC-001's "zero commands run by hand" measurable, given that the modification itself is an action? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK036 Does every functional requirement trace to at least one success criterion, and does every success criterion trace back to a requirement? [Traceability]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK037 Are requirements defined for the recovery flow after a formatting failure — what state the file is left in, and whether a partially rewritten file is possible? [Gap, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK038 Are requirements specified for two modifications to the same file in rapid succession, where the second begins before the first is formatted? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK039 Are requirements defined for the case where the repository is in a state the checks cannot compute a file list from at all? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the exclusion half's rollback path considered — if the equivalence proof fails after the declarations are consolidated, are requirements stated for reverting? [Gap, Recovery Flow]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK041 Is the assumption that the existing definitions of conformance and scope are correct stated as an assumption rather than relied on silently? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the assumption that formatting "completes quickly enough not to be noticeable" quantified, or left as a qualitative expectation? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK043 Is the dependency on the repository's own self-test — named by SC-005, SC-010 and SC-007 as the verification vehicle — documented as a dependency? [Dependency, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK044 Is the resolved assumption about status-message frequency traceable to a requirement, or does it live only in the Assumptions section? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK028 and CHK029 are the two items most likely to be real conflicts rather than wording gaps. Both concern the interaction between the feature's two halves, and both were introduced by folding the scope refactor into a feature whose §FR-003 was written for the formatting half alone. Resolve them before planning rather than during it.
- CHK002, CHK005 and CHK010 are the sharpest instances of the pattern the reviewer asked to be flagged: a requirement whose satisfaction and whose total failure produce the same observable result.
